name: Ortur Laser Master 3 10W
tldr: The 10W Laser Master 3 is Ortur's lower-power SKU on the same frame. Ideal for learning and engraving; cutters should choose the 20W version.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Basic set at $299.99 on Ortur's store in October 2026, less than half the price of the stronger LM3
Full 400 × 400 mm working area, per Ortur
Wi-Fi and USB control on the LM3 platform
cons: Photo fills of ~20–42 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo takes ~15–23 min
Cutting slows to ~2–3 mm/s on 3 mm wood
Ortur only advertises the free Air Pump 1.0 with the higher-power LM3 set
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 10W SKU on Ortur Laser Master 3. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

editorialDepth.advantages: Ortur Laser Master 3 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 5 mm+ cutting in production: see 20W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: How much does the LM3 10W cost compared with the 20W?
faq.answer: On Ortur's store in October 2026 the LM3 10W basic set was $299.99 and the 20W basic set $639.99, the latter with a free Air Pump 1.0. Both sit inside our tracked $140–1,740 range, which spans used units up to Ortur's all-in-one bundles.

faq.question: What can the LM3 10W cut?
faq.answer: In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 8–12 min at 2–3 mm/s. Basswood up to about 5 mm and thin black acrylic are possible in several passes. Ortur publishes one-pass cutting demos only for the 20W module.

faq.question: LM3 10W or 20W: which one suits me?
faq.answer: Take the 10W for engraving-led work on a budget: it keeps the full 400 × 400 mm area, while Ortur lists 400 × 380 mm for the 20W. Take the 20W if you cut regularly: it handles our 3 mm square in about 5–8 min and Ortur demonstrates 10 mm plywood in one pass, for roughly $340 more.

standoutFeatures.title: LM3 platform at entry price
standoutFeatures.body: $299.99 for the basic set in October 2026, with the same LM3 frame and controller as the costlier version.

standoutFeatures.title: Full 400 × 400 mm bed
standoutFeatures.body: Ortur lists the full 400 × 400 mm area for this module, slightly larger than with the stronger head.
